transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2027-10-05
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood CSM), Jordan (Apollo VP Eng), Aisha (Head of ML), Ben (Platform Eng), Samir (Procurement)

Summary:
Quick QBR-style checkpoint to reconcile adoption numbers, run through cost drivers, triage recent reliability incidents (burst latency spikes around 09/29), and align on next steps for a private deployment pilot and a committed capacity conversation.

Topics Covered:
- Usage trends and top growth routes (conversational triage and batch-insights jobs)
- Unit economics: token mix, embeddings vs generation, caching impact
- Reliability incidents: analysis of 09/29 latency spike and mitigation
- Roadmap: pilot timeline for Private + KMS onboarding, and Dedicated capacity pricing options
- Security questions and procurement timing

Transcript Body:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone thanks for joining, I think we have about an hour, wanted to run through usage, costs, the reliability blip last week and then talk next steps on pilot. Jordan, do you want to kick off with what success looks like for Apollo this quarter?
[00:14] Jordan (Apollo VP Eng): Yeah thanks Maya. For us Q4 is about stabilization and predictable unit cost. We've got adoption across two product teams — triage chat is the big one and a scheduled-batch insights pipeline. Key metrics for us are 95th percentile latency under 800ms for chat, and cost-per-1000-requests for the batch job under $X (we're still modeling).
[00:35] Aisha (Head of ML): And from ML side accuracy degradation is also a concern, we saw some drift when we moved prompts last month. We're looking for a way to run controlled rollouts without inflating cost.
[00:48] Priya (Redwood CSM): Great, thanks. We pulled a usage export for the last 90 days and some high-level econ. Diego, do you want to share the latency/cost snapshot?
[00:59] Diego (Redwood SE): Sure. Quick caveat — this is aggregated from your token-level export and our internal logs, and there are some label mismatches so some route names map loosely. But high level: total tokens for the triage route grew 42% month-over-month, embeddings usage is steady but small compared to generation, and caching is shaving off an estimated 18% of token load once enabled for certain routes.
[01:25] Ben (Platform Eng): The caching we rolled out is partial, we didn't apply prefix caching to multi-turn flows because of context concerns.
[01:32] Diego (Redwood SE): Right, and that explains some of the burst behavior — prefix cache misses plus simultaneous rehydration of KV caches during peak created a spike. We correlate that with the 09/29 event Jordan mentioned.
[01:45] Jordan (Apollo VP Eng): On 09/29 our customers saw chat responses slow to 2s+ for about 12 minutes during a spike. It affected conversion for triage flows.
[01:56] Maya (Redwood AE): That's the incident Diego looked at, correct? What were root causes and short-term mitigations?
[02:04] Diego (Redwood SE): Root cause looked like a confluence: large prefix misses from a change in prompt templates, a small autoscale threshold for the dedicated job, and a backend retry storm from a client library we updated that retried aggressively. Mitigation steps we recommend: temporary increase burst pool, enable sticky caching for session tokens, and pin a client library to the previous non-retrying version.
[02:28] Samir (Procurement): From procurement timeline, we need to understand committed spend and SLA before we can sign. Any rough numbers for committed capacity vs pay-as-you-go?
[02:40] Maya (Redwood AE): We'll send a side-by-side. Quick preview: committed reserved capacity reduces effective per-token by ~30% at the bands you're seeing, and we have an intermediate 'burst bundle' option for seasonal peaks. We'll include examples in the worksheet.
[02:57] Aisha (Head of ML): Can you also include the quality/regression guardrails? We don't want quantization to impact our top-level accuracy.
[03:07] Diego (Redwood SE): Absolutely — we'll recommend quant profiles per route. For triage chat we suggest FP16 or 4-bit quant for non-critical routes but keep high-precision for the canonical prompt variants and for evaluation checks. We'll include sample evals to measure prompt-level deltas.
[03:25] Priya (Redwood CSM): Jordan, do you have the timeline for pilot — when can you provide pre-prod access for the SE run?
[03:31] Jordan (Apollo VP Eng): We could open a pre-prod cluster mid-October, say 10/18, but need the security checklist completed before then.
[03:38] Maya (Redwood AE): Good — we'll plan for a private deployment pilot 10/18. Diego, can you own the runbook?
[03:44] Diego (Redwood SE): Yes, I'll create a runbook that includes traffic shaping, KV cache warm-up, and latency SLO validations.
[03:50] Ben (Platform Eng): On KMS: we use Keysight (internal) via a vault-backed HSM — we need to validate Redwood's support for customer-managed keys and that logs can be forwarded to our SIEM.
[03:59] Diego (Redwood SE): We support KMS integrations and syslog/audit forwarding. Priya, we'll include the security matrix and required logs in the packet.
[04:09] Priya (Redwood CSM): Noted — we'll attach SOC 2 and ISO docs, and a short note on KMS options.
[04:15] Jordan (Apollo VP Eng): One thing on cost: embeddings for our recommender are relatively inexpensive, but batch transforms are causing sustained consumption overnight. Any suggestion to shift cost profile?
[04:26] Diego (Redwood SE): For batch: consider off-peak scheduling and increased batching size. Also, enable cache for deterministic transforms and use a cheaper model variant for non-critical scoring. We'll include a model-suggested mapping.
[04:40] Aisha (Head of ML): About rollouts — can Redwood support canary routing per model version so we can route 5% of traffic to a new quantized model and evaluate metrics?
[04:49] Maya (Redwood AE): Yes, rollouts and A/B are supported. We'll walk through how to set weights and automatic fallback if latency or accuracy drifts beyond thresholds.
[04:59] [05:00] Diego (Redwood SE): Also, for the 09/29 spike we saw an odd correlation where a single job triggered many small sequential requests that weren't batched well. Rewriting that job to bundle prompts into a single call reduces overhead substantially.
[05:15] Ben (Platform Eng): We'll look into batching at application layer. That might require some refactor but should be doable.
[05:23] Jordan (Apollo VP Eng): Procurement: Samir, any constraints on contract terms?
[05:28] Samir (Procurement): We need standard auditability, a 99.9% uptime target for Dedicated, and liability language. Also, approval cadence is two weeks once pricing is confirmed.
[05:39] Maya (Redwood AE): Understood; we'll include SLA language and a proposed cadence for legal review.
[05:44] Priya (Redwood CSM): Quick walkthrough of the usage dashboard — we pushed a custom view for Apollo that highlights top routes, token mix, and a latency heatmap. Jordan, you should have access; let us know if anything's off.
[05:57] Jordan (Apollo VP Eng): I can see it now, thanks. The heatmap shows a consistent 450-700ms baseline, with the 09/29 peaks up near 2s.
[06:09] Maya (Redwood AE): Ok let's walk through the pilot plan; timeline sketch: security sign-off by 10/11, pre-prod test on 10/18, pilot run for two weeks, then decision on committed capacity by end of October. Is that fair?
[06:23] Jordan (Apollo VP Eng): That works if we get the security packet quick.
[06:28] Aisha (Head of ML): On the evaluation — can Redwood run our A/B eval harness to compute KL divergence and answer-level F1 for the two model variants?
[06:36] Diego (Redwood SE): Yes, we can run your harness in a controlled environment; we'll produce per-prompt deltas and a regression report.
[06:43] Samir (Procurement): About pricing examples — we need both a committed 12-month and a no-commit monthly option so we can model different scenarios.
[06:51] Maya (Redwood AE): We'll provide both. Also include a sensitivity table for token price vs 10/20/50% growth scenarios.
[06:59] [07:00] Jordan (Apollo VP Eng): Any blockers on the Redwood side to start the pre-prod run?
[07:05] Diego (Redwood SE): We need the export of last 60 days of traffic, the pre-prod endpoint, and access to your SIEM for log-forwarding test.
[07:13] Jordan (Apollo VP Eng): We'll send the export and open a short-lived SIEM ingestion for the test.
[07:18] Priya (Redwood CSM): Action recap — Priya to send SOC2/ISO, Maya to send pricing worksheet, Diego to own the runbook, Jordan to share export. We'll capture exact dates after the call.
[07:31] Ben (Platform Eng): One quick technical ask — can Redwood expose token-level traces so we can tie slow requests back to specific model invocations?
[07:40] Diego (Redwood SE): Yes, we have token-level tracing and request IDs. We'll show an example trace during the runbook session.
[07:47] Aisha (Head of ML): Regarding quantization, if we see small accuracy drop for 4-bit we want an automated rollback. Is that doable?
[07:55] Diego (Redwood SE): Yep — automatic fallback to a higher-precision model on regression events is supported. We'll include threshold settings.
[08:02] Jordan (Apollo VP Eng): Last thing — can we get a simple 1-pager for execs summarizing the economics and risk tradeoffs?
[08:09] Maya (Redwood AE): We'll produce a one-pager and an appendix with the detail.

-- Mid-call interruptions and clarifications --
[22:10] Maya (Redwood AE): Sorry hang on, my audio cut, back now.
[22:16] Jordan (Apollo VP Eng): No worries. I wanted to ask about retention — how long do you keep token logs by default?
[22:25] Priya (Redwood CSM): Default retention is 90 days, but we can extend retention for enterprise accounts and we also support log forwarding to your S3 or SIEM.
[22:33] Ben (Platform Eng): We will want to store request/response pairs for 180 days for audit. Is that supported?
[22:40] Diego (Redwood SE): Supported via log-forwarding; Redwood hosted retention can be extended but usually forwarding to customer-managed storage is recommended for that window.

-- Incident deep dive (approx 30 minutes in) --
[32:05] Diego (Redwood SE): For the 09/29 window we pulled three traces. Two were large cache miss storms, one was a hogging job that produced serial calls. We recommend a temporary burst pool increase during your peak hour (14:00 UTC) while we implement session-level sticky caching.
[32:25] Jordan (Apollo VP Eng): If we bump burst pool what happens to cost?
[32:31] Maya (Redwood AE): Short-term: you'll see a modest bump for that hour, we'll quantify in the worksheet. Long-term: caching and batching will more than offset that if implemented.
[32:40] Ben (Platform Eng): What about autoscale settings, are those editable per-route?
[32:45] Diego (Redwood SE): Yes per-route autoscale and priority tiers are editable. We can set SLO-driven priorities so the triage chat gets precedence over batch jobs during contention.

-- Closing (last 10 minutes) --
[52:12] Maya (Redwood AE): Okay, wrapping up. Quick recap of deliverables: Maya to send pricing worksheet (10/08), Priya share security docs (SOC2, ISO, KMS notes) (10/06), Diego runbook and benchmark plan (10/15), Jordan to share token export and confirm pre-prod access (10/10). Any additions?
[52:36] Jordan (Apollo VP Eng): Please include example SLA language.
[52:40] Samir (Procurement): And procurement will need a list of subcontractors and data flows for review.
[52:47] Priya (Redwood CSM): We'll include that in the security packet.
[52:52] Maya (Redwood AE): Great. We'll follow up in writing and schedule the SE-runbook kick-off. Thanks everyone.
[52:59] Aisha (Head of ML): Thanks all.
[53:02] Ben (Platform Eng): Thanks.
[53:05] Samir (Procurement): Thanks.

End of meeting.

Notes on transcription: occasional mislabeling and small ASR errors (proper nouns, model variant names), timestamps approximate.
